title: Run the project's notebook cells on the Notebook page, in a kernel with the training rows only
request: After the fixes, how can we run cells? Can it be implemented? (The page said running cells here was not built.)
spec: The owner's decisions, 2026-10-20: any signed-in member may run cells for now (local-only later); the kernel gets the training rows only.
plan: A Jupyter kernel per project, started on the first cell, shut down when idle.
The kernel's folder holds the table's training rows under the name the notebook reads.
Run the server's own cell for an index; refuse the holdout cell.
Keep every run whole; wire Run, Run all, Restart and outputs on the page.

decisions.decision: The kernel reads a copy of the table with the engine's training rows only, in the table's own columns.
decisions.why: The notebook's cells then run unchanged and the holdout never enters the kernel: the owner's choice.

decisions.decision: The engine keeps each prepared row's place in the loaded table (Prepared.source_rows).
decisions.why: The split's indices point at prepared rows (filtered, reordered, sampled); the copy must be rows of the raw file.

decisions.decision: A cell runs the source the server generates for that index, never code from the page.
decisions.why: The page cannot send arbitrary code through this route.

decisions.decision: The kernel runs the server's own Python, without any key, token or database address in its environment.
decisions.why: A cell's code must not read the server's secrets; a kernel found elsewhere on the machine ran other libraries.

decisions.decision: Run and restart are read-level routes.
decisions.why: The owner chose any signed-in member; the safer rule is in the roadmap for a shared deployment.

change: dclab_rnd/studio/kernels.py; studio/engine.py (source_rows); studio/export.py (cell roles; the positive class as the engine picks it); routes run, restart and kernel status; guard; services; server shutdown; the Notebook page; tests/test_notebook_cells.py.

findings.defect: The exported notebook's cross-validation cell failed with one class.
findings.scenario: A solution with no positive label: the notebook compared the target to the string 'None', so every row was 0.
findings.cause: The export wrote the unset positive label as text; the engine takes the last value in order.
findings.fix: The export writes the engine's rule into the notebook.

findings.defect: The kernel ran another environment's Python.
findings.cause: The python3 kernelspec resolved to one installed elsewhere on the machine.
findings.fix: A kernelspec of the server's own interpreter.

measurements.name: Run all on a real project in the browser
measurements.gate: every cell before the holdout runs, the holdout cell is refused, the kernel has the training rows only
measurements.result: 6 code cells ran (1,200 training rows, CV mean 0.866); the holdout cell shows runs in the workflow; the kernel table holds no holdout row

outcome: A person can run the project's notebook on its page, with the holdout read only by the workflow.
lessons: Pin a kernel to the server's own interpreter: the default kernelspec may be any Python on the machine.
risks: Any signed-in member can run code as the server's user until the sandbox step; a project with a joined label file runs in the person's own Jupyter.
